answers.gloss: A traffic-engineering node in a layer-specific network; it represents the TE abstraction of a forwarding, switching, or transport-domain node.
answers.example: ROADM R1 in the OTN layer.
answers.relations: It is part of i.tetopo and hosts termination points such as i.tp; node-internal connectivity may be constrained by i.cmatrix.

answers.gloss: A termination point on a TE node at which a TE link terminates.
answers.example: The termination point on R1 facing R2 for the R1–R2 TE link.
answers.relations: It is on i.tenode and terminates i.telink. A TP may participate in a cross-layer supporting relationship represented by i.stp.

answers.gloss: The supporting relationship by which a client-layer termination point is supported by a server-layer termination point; it represents inter-layer adaptation rather than an ordinary same-layer link.
answers.example: An OTN termination point at R1 supported by an optical-layer termination point at R1.
answers.relations: It relates/supports i.tp across client and server layers and captures the adaptation between those termination-point representations.

answers.gloss: The point at which a TE tunnel originates or terminates—a tunnel trail head. It is tunnel-specific and is not merely an externally advertised service-access point.
answers.example: The A1 trail head of the A1–A3 ODU2 tunnel.
answers.relations: It is on i.tenode and originates or terminates i.tunnel; the opposite TTP is the other tunnel end.

answers.gloss: An end-to-end traffic-engineered tunnel that realizes connectivity for a service. It is the TE construct carrying traffic along an engineered path, not merely the abstract offer of connectivity to a customer.
answers.example: The A1–A3 ODU2 TE tunnel.
answers.relations: It runs between i.ttp endpoints, traverses resources represented by i.tetopo, contains or associates with i.tcep endpoints within nodes, and may be labelled by i.otnlabel.

answers.gloss: An OTN traffic-engineering label that expresses the tributary-slot and tributary-port-number multiplexing structure used to carry a client ODU within a server OTN signal.
answers.example: The TS/TPN allocation carrying an ODU2 within an OTU4.
answers.relations: It labels i.tunnel or its allocated resources and records OTN multiplexing information such as tributary-slot occupancy.

answers.gloss: A node-local connectivity matrix describing which internal connections or cross-connects are permitted among the node's termination points.
answers.example: R2's matrix permitting selected ingress-to-egress OTN cross-connects.
answers.relations: It belongs to i.tenode and constrains permissible internal connectivity among that node's i.tp instances.

answers.gloss: A traffic-engineering link connecting TE nodes in one layer network.
answers.example: The R1–R2 TE link in the OTN layer.
answers.relations: It lies between i.tenode instances, is terminated by i.tp at its ends, and is contained by i.tetopo.

answers.gloss: A layer-specific traffic-engineering network/topology. In this model it denotes one per-layer topology rather than a single undifferentiated multi-layer domain, although multiple such topologies may be related operationally.
answers.example: The OTN layer network containing R1, R2, R3 and their OTN TE links.
answers.relations: It contains i.tenode and i.telink and provides the topology over which i.tunnel is engineered.

answers.gloss: An endpoint of a tunnel connection located within or on a node; it identifies the connection-level endpoint associated with a particular tunnel, rather than a generic physical/link termination.
answers.example: The A1–A3 tunnel's connection endpoint on R1.
answers.relations: It is on i.tenode and is part of or associated with i.tunnel; it is distinct from i.tp, which terminates a TE link, and from i.ttp, which is the tunnel trail head.

answers.gloss: A forwarding, switching, or transport node in the domain's single multi-layer topology. It is not intrinsically a separate per-layer node object.
answers.example: ROADM R1.
answers.relations: It is part of t.topo and owns edge points such as t.ltp; node-local switching constraints may be represented by t.nrg.

answers.gloss: A node-owned edge point at which a topological link terminates.
answers.example: The R1 edge point facing R2.
answers.relations: It is on t.node and terminates t.link. This model does not state that the LTP itself aggregates layer-protocol-specific termination details.

answers.gloss: A distinct link-like object expressing client/server adaptation between layers at a node, rather than an ordinary same-layer topological link.
answers.example: The OTU4/ODU2 adaptation at R1.
answers.relations: It is located at t.node and expresses adaptation characterized by t.lpq. Its endpoints are not explicitly modeled as t.ltp instances in the supplied relations.

answers.gloss: An externally exposed point where a client service accesses the network.
answers.example: The ODU2 client hand-off at A1.
answers.relations: It is on t.node and provides access to t.cs. It is distinct from the connection-specific t.cep; this model specifies no direct t.sip-to-t.ltp relation.

answers.gloss: An offered or requested end-to-end connectivity service across the network, not the underlying engineered tunnel or path that realizes it.
answers.example: The A1–A3 ODU2 connectivity service.
answers.relations: It uses t.sip access points, is realized through connection endpoints represented by t.cep, and is provided over t.topo.

answers.gloss: A qualifier describing a signal's layer and multiplexing structure.
answers.example: ODU2 mapped into an OTU4 server signal.
answers.relations: It qualifies t.cs and is referenced by t.translink adaptation. It describes multiplexing/layer structure; it is not defined as a concrete allocated tributary-slot or tributary-port-number resource label.

answers.gloss: A node-local rule group constraining which ports or endpoints may be cross-connected.
answers.example: R2's permitted ingress-to-egress cross-connect rules.
answers.relations: It belongs to t.node and governs permissible internal switching connectivity.

answers.gloss: A topological link between two nodes in the domain topology.
answers.example: The R1–R2 link.
answers.relations: It lies between t.node instances, is terminated by t.ltp at its ends, and is contained in t.topo. The model places links in one multi-layer topology rather than requiring a separate topology object for each layer.

answers.gloss: The single multi-layer topology describing the network domain.
answers.example: The OTN-over-optical domain topology.
answers.relations: It contains t.node and t.link and is the topology over which t.cs is provided. Unlike a necessarily per-layer topology, one t.topo may describe multiple related layers.

answers.gloss: A connection-specific endpoint located within or on a node.
answers.example: The endpoint on R1 for the A1–A3 service connection.
answers.relations: It is on t.node and forms part of t.cs's realization. It is distinct from t.ltp, which terminates a topological link, and from t.sip, which is an external service-access point.
